test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 27 Feb 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are given followed by two conclusions I and II. You have to consider the two statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts and then decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follows/follow from the given statements.

**Statements:**

1. All Trees are Flowers 

2. No Flower is Plant. 

3. Some Plants are Roots.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some Roots are Trees. 

II. Some Plants are Trees.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follow.

solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9f47834915effbf861cae57dbe02047cb08cfa63c157c5c8a23c434a296e87b6.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some Roots are Trees → Does not follow (As all Trees are Flowers, no Flower is Plant and some Plants are Roots. So it is possible but not definite.)

II. Some Plants are Trees → Does not follow (As all Trees are Flowers and no Flower is Plant. As whole trees comes in flowers which cannot be plants, therefore it is false.)

∴ Here, Neither conclusion I nor II follow.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2"
